hints: Focus on what structural isomers must share, the same molecular formula but a different arrangement of atoms.
Count carbons, hydrogens and oxygens for each pair, remembering that $\text{COOH}$ already contains one C, two O and one H.
Look for the pair with the same atom count but one straight chain and one branched chain, not two ways of writing the same molecule.
walkthrough:
**Recall the test for structural isomers**

Remember, structural isomers have identical molecular formulae but different structural formulae. So we must check both the atom count and the arrangement.

Rule:
$$\text{same molecular formula + different structure = structural isomers}$$

**Expand and count the key pair**

Take $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$. This is a straight chain of 4 carbons: 3 in the chain plus 1 in $\text{COOH}$, giving $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}_2$. This is butanoic acid.

Now take $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{CHCOOH}$. This is a branched chain with 3 carbons plus 1 in $\text{COOH}$, also giving $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}_2$. This is 2-methylpropanoic acid.

**Compare arrangement and conclude**

Both molecules have $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}_2$, so the formula matches. But one is straight chain and the other is branched at carbon 2, so the connectivity is different.

This is chain isomerism, so this pair correctly represents structural isomers.

options.A: Both $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(CH}_3\text{)COOH}$ and $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{CHCOOH}$ expand to the same structure, 2-methylpropanoic acid with formula $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}_2$. They are two ways of writing the identical molecule, not isomers with different arrangements.
options.B: Both $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(COOH)CH}_3$ and $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{CHCOOH}$ are the same branched acid, 2-methylpropanoic acid. Writing the $\text{COOH}$ group in the middle does not change the connectivity, so this is the same compound twice.
options.C: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$ is $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}_2$ but $\text{CH}_3\text{CHCOOH}$ as written has only 3 carbons and an incomplete valence on the middle carbon. Different atom counts (and an invalid formula) can never be isomers.
options.D: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$ is straight-chain butanoic acid and $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{CHCOOH}$ is branched 2-methylpropanoic acid. Both have molecular formula $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}_2$ but different carbon skeletons, so they are a classic pair of chain structural isomers.
